## Introduction

We ask how strongly health and well-being are associated across the
studies included in the selected `HealthWellbeing` dataset version.
The input consists of study summaries from the teaching example in
*Doing Meta-Analysis with R: A Hands-On Guide*.
[Section 4.2.4, Correlations](https://doing-meta.guide/pooling-es#correlations)

```{r health-report-input, include = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
# The summary path is relative to the project root, wherever Quarto runs.
summary_file <- here::here(params$summary_file)
if (!file.exists(summary_file)) {
  stop("Summary missing. Run the pipeline or use Get back on track in the Quarto lesson.")
}
result <- utils::read.csv(summary_file, colClasses = "character")
stopifnot(nrow(result) == 1L, result$effect_scale == "ZCOR")
stopifnot(
  all(c("tau_method", "interval_method") %in% names(result)),
  !anyNA(c(result$tau_method, result$interval_method)),
  all(nzchar(c(result$tau_method, result$interval_method)))
)
numeric_fields <- c(
  "pooled_r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "confidence_level",
  "tau2", "i2_percent", "prediction_lower", "prediction_upper", "prediction_level"
)
required_fields <- c(
  numeric_fields, "prediction_method", "data_source", "raw_md5", "data_file_md5",
  "data_filter", "data_scope", "predictive_model_version", "pipeline_md5"
)
if (!all(required_fields %in% names(result))) {
  stop("Summary is from an earlier exercise. Run the current pipeline and render again.")
}
result[numeric_fields] <- lapply(result[numeric_fields], as.numeric)

tau_method <- switch(
  result$tau_method,
  REML = "restricted maximum likelihood (REML)",
  PM = "the Paule–Mandel method (PM)",
  DL = "the DerSimonian–Laird method (DL)",
  result$tau_method
)
interval_method <- switch(
  result$interval_method,
  HK = "the Hartung–Knapp method (HK)",
  KR = "the Kenward–Roger method (KR)",
  classic = "a normal approximation (classic)",
  result$interval_method
)

pipeline_md5 <- result[["pipeline_md5"]]
```

## Methods

The analysis pools Pearson correlations on Fisher's z scale with a
random-effects model. The pipeline estimates between-study variance
using `r tau_method` and calculates a confidence interval using
`r interval_method`. It transforms the estimate and interval limits
back to the correlation scale. The prediction interval uses the
`r result$prediction_method` method. Similarity of effect definitions and
independence of study estimates are assumptions of this analysis.

## Results

The analysis combined `r result$studies` studies. The pooled
correlation was `r sprintf("%.3f", result$pooled_r)` with a
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * result$confidence_level)` confidence interval
from `r sprintf("%.3f", result$ci_lower)` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", result$ci_upper)`.

Between-study variance was `r sprintf("%.3f", result$tau2)` on the
Fisher z scale, and I² was `r sprintf("%.1f%%", result$i2_percent)`.
The `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * result$prediction_level)` prediction interval
was `r sprintf("%.3f", result$prediction_lower)` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", result$prediction_upper)`.

The confidence interval describes uncertainty in the average association.
The prediction interval is wider and describes the range of plausible
true associations in a comparable setting under this model. These
observational estimates do not establish causation.

-   Selected input MD5: `r result$data_file_md5`
-   Inclusion rule: `r result$data_filter` (`r result$data_scope`)
-   Predictive model pin version: `r result$predictive_model_version`
-   Pipeline script MD5: `r pipeline_md5`
-   R version: `r result$r_version`
-   *meta* version: `r result$meta_version`
-   Effect scale: `r result$effect_scale`
-   Variance estimator: `r result$tau_method`
-   Interval method: `r result$interval_method`

The predictive model is a separately pinned regression trained on the same
checked data. The meta-analysis uses the study correlations and sample sizes
directly.
